# PS Børne- og Ungdomspsykiatrisk Ambulatorier

PS Børne- og Ungdomspsykiatrisk Ambulatorier is a Danish child and adolescent psychiatric outpatient service tracked in the national ADHD-databasen (ADHD database) report covering the period 01.04.2024–31.03.2025. The unit appears repeatedly in the quality-indicator tables that measure how well ADHD assessment and treatment pathways for children and young people follow the national clinical standards set for Danish psychiatric departments [^src1][^src2][^src3][^src4].

Its most significant data point concerns Indikator 2b, which measures the frequency of manualized diagnostic interviews or environmental observation during ADHD assessment. On this indicator the unit achieved only 39% fulfilment (151 out of 392 cases, confidence interval 34–44) [^src1], far below the national development target of 90% described in the surrounding report context [^src1]. This places PS Børne- og Ungdomspsykiatrisk Ambulatorier among the departments falling well short of the goal, a pattern the report links to broader implementation barriers such as geographic challenges, registration problems, and variable waiting times affecting ADHD assessment quality nationwide [^src1].

The unit also appears in a related but distinct data line, also on page 16, showing 10 out of 24 cases (42%, CI 22–63) for what the table presents alongside the 2b figures, reflecting the report's parallel tracking of Indikator 2a and 2b results across regions and departments [^src1]. Elsewhere in the report, the unit is recorded with 26% fulfilment (107 out of 416 cases, CI 22–30) on another indicator table [^src2], a markedly low figure of 7% (CI 0–32) on a further indicator [^src3], and a notably higher figure of 87% (13 out of 15 cases, CI 60–98) on yet another table [^src4] — illustrating substantial variation in the unit's performance depending on which specific quality measure is being assessed.

These figures sit within a wider national picture: the ADHD database's Indikator 2b and Indikator 3 results show only 51% and 27% fulfilment respectively at the national level, both far under the 90% development goal, prompting the steering group to revise both indicators to better reflect current clinical practice. Other indicators discussed in the same report — including Indikator 10 (assessment of social support needs for adults, 37% national fulfilment) and Indikator 11 (ADHD medication within 120 days of adult treatment start) — provide further context for how child and adolescent, and adult, ADHD services are being measured across Denmark, though those specific figures are not attributed to PS Børne- og Ungdomspsykiatrisk Ambulatorier in the supplied data.
